title: Day 41 of making fishing rpg in unity using claude ai
author: ForkedPush
selftext:
Some work I have done on the character creator this week.

Improved character visuals and animations

Most of the improvements are not in the demo yet but you can play the current version here:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5351000/I\_Just\_Wanted\_to\_Fish\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5351000/I_Just_Wanted_to_Fish_Demo/)

comments.author: MasterSlayer11

replies.body: Thanks, mostly blender(with blender mcp) and good shaders.

replies.author: BoinkyMcZoinky
replies.body: Do you still have to do a lot of manual work with it?

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body:
not too much with models, but a lot of manual work with shaders, lighting, post processing etc.   
but the most time consuming manual parts are play testing, level design and game design.

replies.author: SvenPatrick
replies.body: Intresting. I would have assumed it's the other way around. I see Claude doing a great job optimizing Shaders but sometimes I'm having a hard time in letting Claude build simpe low poly models (not talking about rigging) and your game looks great!

comments.author: xaeru
comments.body: I installed the demo, but I wasn't able to catch any fish. I just ended up dropping the game.

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: Sorry to hear that, I am improving the difficulty curve and onboarding for new players.

replies.author: xaeru
replies.body: I really liked the game, so I'm definitely giving it another shot. Just FYI, there weren't any tips or tutorials, so I honestly had no idea what I was doing wrong.

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: Honestly I was thinking if the players discover the mechanics themselves then it would be more rewarding for them(But my implementation was wrong and I think a bit of rework to tutorial wouldn't disturb the first time impression). But I messed up the onboarding it seems. I believe I can still achieve that with a bit of handholding at the start without boring the players too much. Additionally I also made quite a bit of balance changes to difficulty of the fish so it will be easier at the start. On the bright side, the demo is there to actually let the players play test and give me feedback, so thank you for the feedback!

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: I will probably update the demo this week

comments.author: StandardCategory5153
comments.body:
Looks great! I would suggest looking at WEBFISHING for more side-objectices and multiplayer support.

Claude can use steam lobbies and p2p support in a day.

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: I am planning to implement some form of online feature, at least you will be able to fish with your friends. Thanks for the tips

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body:
Great! Also -- you should hardcore test the onboarding and FTUE experience of your game.

The game art looks great, the idea is simple and easy to understand. The theme feels cozy and inviting... But the FTUE is hard and confusing... 

This tells me this is probably your first game as the design lead. You clearly understand art so I assume you have some kind of professional artist background. In traditional game dev artist led games can easily suffer because the game focus on art and looks and feel too much and not enough on pure fun gameplay.

Ultimately you are making a game, not a youtube animated video. You nailed the look. Focus all your energy on making a truly enjoyable fishing experience that starts simple and easy to understand and unlocks deeper and deeper as you go down the rabbit hole (when the user is hooked).

I'm a pro who has lead multiple successful commercial games, so just saying all of this to help support you! AI dev has changed game dev forever and I'm here for it.

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: I actually have background on game design. The problem is that the demo is only playtested by me, and it had little time in oven. I agree with your points tho, it definetely needs more work on the onboarding. I want to keep some aspects of the game design as I envisioned, otherwise the game would turn into something without an identity. On the other hand I am not too stubborn to not listen quaility feedback so it is appreciated

comments.author: hello-xworld
comments.body:
OP, your game looks incredible!

Though are you concerned about copycats? I’ve seen you post here a lot with your progress. And I love that you are transparent with your game dev journey. I’m also working on my own game but have been hesitant posting about it because of copycats.

How do you plan to deal with them?

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: Thank you! I am concerned, tbh it might seem I am sharing too much progress but I am only sharing a fraction of what I am doing outside of what is already in demo. It is difficult times, you have to share your game to gather interest and advertise it but you also have to be careful about copy cats too

replies.author: hello-xworld
replies.body: If this is only a fraction of the game then that’s incredible. Keep at it!

comments.author: ShockiL1ne
comments.body: Game looks amazing! How did you go about the animations? Did you use a specific workflow/mcp? I tried third party/bought animations but they dont really fit my models. Then I tried blender mcp based on a reference video but the animations need lots of work afterwards.. Yours are looking good so I was curious. :)

replies.author: ForkedPush
replies.body: Hey thanks, majority of the animations are made by opus 5.5 in blender using blender mcp. I have used a few mixamo animations too. I made claude make me a tool in unity that I can create key poses for difficult animatiıns like carrying stuff, and hand poses, arm poses etc. honestly theres like some manual work and some blender mcp work it takes a lot of time for claude to create something I can use in the game. Even today I keep refining animations
